title: The 6 wire-path pins (incl. the load-bearing cost-immunity pin) are not exercised by any ci-local gate — suite stays 10/10 even if they rot
evidence: "Core unit tests (the determinism + topology contracts)|odin test core"  (the only odin-test entry in the GATES array; .github/workflows/ci.yml:70 likewise runs only "run: odin test core"; the pins live in app/render/wire_path_test.odin, and `odin build app` never compiles _test.odin files)
detail: Briefing acceptance 2 chains 'Cost-immunity + determinism pins green; ... tools/ci-local.sh 10/10'. The pins pass today (verified: odin test app/render = 6/6) but no gate runs or even compiles them, so a cost-immunity regression would not fail the local suite the guards call ground truth.
recommended_fix: Add an 11th gate (or extend gate 2) running `odin test app/render`, mirroring it in .github/workflows/ci.yml per the file's step-for-step parity rule.

title: PR body's pixel-level determinism proof (render twice → identical SHA-256) has no in-tree artifact — claim not reproducible from the shipped code
evidence:
- **Determinism:** pixel-level proof — the routed gate frame rendered twice produces identical SHA-256 hashes.
  a pixel-level determinism check (two renders of the same frame, byte-identical hashes).  (grep for sha256/hash/render-twice across harness/, app/, tools/ finds only raylib's ComputeSHA256 binding; harness/wire_preview.odin renders each gate frame exactly once via single render_scene_frame calls and never hashes)
detail: The guards explicitly asked to verify this claim is 'actually reproducible in-tree'. Path-level determinism IS pinned (test_path_determinism, green), but the stronger pixel-level SHA-256 claim is backed by no verb, test, or script in the diff — it rests on an unrecorded manual run.
recommended_fix: Either add a harness verb/test that renders a routed frame twice and compares hashes, or reword the PR body to attribute the pixel check as a one-off manual verification.

title: Ribbon-fan pin looks up nonexistent node id 8 and discards the error — passes only because the failed lookup's zero-value slot 0 coincides with the router
evidence:
rs, _ := pp.node_slot(&s.topology, 8)
		nw := node_world(&s.topology, rs, 26.0)  — wire_setup spawns exactly ids 0..5 (rt id 0, n1..n4 ids 1..4, host id 5); core/topology.odin:93: `return 0, false` on lookup failure
detail: node_slot(topo, 8) fails (ids only go to 5), returns slot 0 with ok=false discarded; slot 0 happens to be the router, so the apex-distance assertion measures the right node by coincidence. Violates the errors-are-values rule and silently tests the wrong node if the fixture ever reorders.
recommended_fix: Use the real router id: `rs, ok := pp.node_slot(&s.topology, 0)` with testing.expect on ok (or reuse `rt` from the setup), never discarding the lookup result.
